title: Zafira — GLP Grey Fog VSL Breakdown

cards.text: ZAFIRA — GLP GREY FOG VSL BREAKDOWN

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Reference: Zafira Organics, Meta, 4:18 vertical VSL-style UGC (110 days running, ~500 ads live from this advertiser). One narrator carries a first-person Mounjaro story start to finish; roughly every 3 seconds the edit cuts to a repurposed UGC/stock clip of a DIFFERENT woman acting out the exact line being spoken. Story arc: flat-and-exhausted → 'it's a real, common side effect' → receptor-sensitivity mechanism → one-formula discovery via Reddit → wanting-to-cook-again transformation. The product appears once, at 3:46. Script below is verbatim and linear; frames are attached only to action/b-roll beats — talking-head stretches are script-only by design.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I feel like we should actually talk about how mentally exhausting GLP-1s can be

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Curiosity + validation — hook. Direct-address 'we should talk about' frames a taboo being broken

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: ...and why it actually happens.
Woman slumped in leather armchair, eyes closed, checked out

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Recognition — the viewer sees her own 3pm slump before a single claim is made

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Because three months into Mounjaro,
Different woman prepping a Mounjaro pen at home under a ceiling fan

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Credibility — real pen, real ritual. Signals 'I'm one of you' to GLP-1 users

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I noticed I hadn't gone to the gym in six weeks.
Gray-haired woman from behind, hovering in a bathroom doorway

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Quiet shame — avoidance shown from behind, no face, universal

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I started procrastinating instead of doing stuff.
Slow listless sweeping of a leaf-covered patio

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Listlessness — a chore performed at half-speed, motion without energy

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And the weird part was I didn't even care.
Extreme close-up, eyes closed, hand pressed to cheek, zero affect

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Anhedonia — the thesis of the ad in one face. Flat, not sad

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So I started digging into the research to figure out what was actually happening to me. I wanted to take control of my life again, feel motivated, go to the gym, and lose weight, but be happy at the same time.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Agency turn — narrator energy lifts; the 'but be happy at the same time' line names the impossible tradeoff

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And I did find something that helped me get back on track. And the good thing was it wasn't just some random energy booster or dopamine hack.
Two generic supplement bottles (ENERGY BOOSTER / DOPAMINE SUPPORT) with a red X slapped over them

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: False-solution dismissal — pre-empts the skeptic's 'this is just another pill' objection before the pitch

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It was something that I found directly out of the GLP-1 research,
Fake 'Journal of Metabolic Psychiatry' browser screenshot slides over the narrator

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Borrowed authority — science skin on a UGC ad. ⚠️ Mockup journal, see compliance note

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: and I'm gonna walk you through exactly what it is and why it worked so well when nothing else did.
Green supplement bottle, blurred, with a big red '?' over the label

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Open loop — product teased and withheld. This '?' bottle is the reason the next 3 minutes get watched

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: First, let me tell you how bad it actually got. So I started Mounjaro about seven months ago, and honestly, I think I'm a great responder.
Woman holds three Mounjaro pens fanned out to camera

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Proof of tenure — seven months, three pens. She's not a tourist

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: The weight loss has been working really well for me.
Feet on a bathroom scale reading 60.9

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Concrete win — the drug WORKS. Ad never attacks the medication

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: In the first three months, I lost almost ten percent of my body weight, so that was good.
Mirror selfie, sports bra, mid-loss body, phone covering face

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Honest progress — imperfect real body = trust. Sets up 'so that was good, BUT'

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But what I didn't notice was how the exhaustion and the flat feeling just crept in.
Woman at a window holding a mug, staring at nothing

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The turn — stillness after the wins. 'Crept in' visualized as vacant stare

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It was so gradual. I was living in this fog for weeks, maybe even longer, and I didn't even see it,
Woman in glasses doom-scrolling at a kitchen counter, curled inward

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Fog made visible — screen-sitting as the modern symptom

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: until my husband literally said to me, "You've been different recently." And he was right.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Outside witness — the husband line is the emotional gut-punch; someone else saw it first

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I was not really sad because sadness has some kind of texture to it. I was just flat. I stopped exercising.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Differentiation — 'sadness has texture, I was flat' separates this from depression, keeps it supplement-solvable

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I started losing muscle because of that.
Close-up pinching loose skin on an upper arm

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Fear beat — muscle loss is the GLP-1 user's #1 silent terror. Physical stakes added to emotional ones

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I would sit there with my phone for forty-five minutes before I could do anything around the house.
Woman sunk into a couch at night, face lit by phone

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Specificity — '45 minutes' + the exact posture every viewer recognizes from last night

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And I had a to-do list that just kept growing,
Hand writing an endless to-do list in a spiral notebook

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Accumulating guilt — the list as scoreboard of failure

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: and I'd look at it and feel nothing. And that was the problem. My drive to do anything was just gone.
Woman standing in kitchen, head down, hands braced on counter

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Rock bottom — 'feel nothing' is the problem statement, fully agitated

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But the good thing was, at some point I decided, "No. Enough. I wanna live my life normally again, even on GLP-1. I need my energy and my motivation back."
Woman holds her GLP-1 pen up to camera, resolute

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Decision beat — agency returns. Pen stays in shot: the fix will NOT replace the med

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So I called my friend Lisa from school.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Bridge — warm, personal on-ramp to the authority figure

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: She studied metabolic health after we graduated, and she's been working with GLP-1 patients for the past two years.
Clinical consult scene: woman in white coat across a desk from a patient

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Authority by association — 'friend from school' + white coat = trusted expert without naming a doctor

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And I just told her straight, "Something is off with my mood. I've been very flat recently, and I think it's the medication."

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Patient voice — viewer rehearses the exact sentence she could say to her own doctor

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And she said this is very common, but nobody talks about it.
White-coat woman taking a call at her desk, concerned

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Validation — 'very common, nobody talks about it' = you're not broken, you're under-informed

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: They had the same thing going with her patients, and she showed me multiple studies confirming this is a real side effect.
Collage of four fake news/health headlines linking GLP-1 to emotional flatness, red underlines

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Consensus effect — four 'independent' sources at once. ⚠️ Fabricated mockups, see compliance note

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And this is what she explained to me, and it finally made sense. Like, GLP-1s lower the dopamine you get, so you don't have any interest in food.
Elderly woman poking at a dinner plate, zero appetite

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Mechanism step 1 — the intended effect shown at the dinner table

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But very often it affects things like your motivation or pleasure or your drive to do things overall.
Woman lying in bed mid-day, staring past camera

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Mechanism step 2 — same dial turns down food AND joy. The ad's core reframe

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But here's the part that actually changed how I understood everything. She said the reason some people feel perfectly fine on GLP-1 and others feel like I did comes down to how sensitive your dopamine receptors are.
Glowing 3D brain animation, gold synapses firing

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The mechanism reveal — receptor sensitivity explains 'why her and not me'. Personalizes without blaming the drug

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Like, there's still happiness in your brain, but the question is whether you can feel it or not. She said if I wanna feel fine again,

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Hope reframe — 'happiness is still in there' = nothing is broken, just muted. Sets up the unlock

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: there are specific compounds like saffron, L-theanine, myo-inositol, vitamin D, have been researched specifically for this.
Ingredient bubbles pop over narrator: saffron threads, L-theanine powder

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Ingredient credibility — named actives, shown as real substances not pills

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: ...that have been researched specifically for this.
Lab scientist at a microscope, mask and coat

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Science texture — 30 frames of lab b-roll to laminate 'researched' onto the ingredient list

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: They make your brain feel the dopamine again, but they don't interact with the medication.
3D anatomy animation: nervous system lighting up from brain down the spine

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Safety + payoff in one line — 'feel it again' visualized as the body switching back on. 'Doesn't interact' kills the #1 fear

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: After that conversation, I went down a Reddit rabbit hole to see if there's something out there that wouldn't be five different pills I have to take.
Phone screen: r/GLP1Support thread about fatigue and taking 5 different things

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Peer proof begins — discovery moved from expert to community. ⚠️ Fabricated thread

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Spent maybe two weeks just researching, and then in one thread I found this protocol called Zafira.
Reddit comment with 1.7k upvotes naming ZAFIRA, highlighted

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: The reveal — product named by a 'stranger with no agenda', not by the narrator. Two weeks = diligence

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It had everything Lisa recommended, but also ginger for the nausea
Woman gagging + bowl of fresh ginger overlay

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Bonus benefit 1 — nausea, the other GLP-1 misery, handled with visual comedy

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: and magnesium for the sleep and cortisol, all of it in one formula made specifically for people on GLP-1s.
Bowl of magnesium flakes + green-to-red gauge dial overlay

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Bonus benefit 2 + positioning — 'made specifically for people on GLP-1s' is the category claim

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So luckily, I didn't have to take five different pills and guess at dosages.
Five assorted loose pills circled in red

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Consolidation close — 5 pills vs 1 formula. Convenience is the conversion lever

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And after I tried it, I think around day five or six, I already noticed some small changes. I was standing in the kitchen, and I actually wanted to cook dinner.
Woman pauses in kitchen mid-prep, looking up, deciding

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: First green shoot — humble, believable timeline (day 5-6, 'small changes'), not a miracle

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I wasn't hungry, but I just wanted to make something nice for everyone.
Same woman now actively assembling a casserole

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Wanting ≠ hunger — desire returned while appetite suppression kept working. The whole promise in one scene

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: By week two, I started exercising again. I knocked out a whole to-do list on a Saturday morning that would have taken me three weeks before.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Momentum montage (talking head) — callbacks to gym + to-do list pains, now inverted

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Things just became fun again. Now it's been four months and I'm still taking Zafira and losing weight on Mounjaro,
Smiling woman holds a single capsule up to camera

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Product's only real appearance — one capsule, held by a happy customer, 3:46 into a 4:18 ad

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: but the difference is that I actually feel like a person while I'm doing it.
Woman runs both hands through her hair, lit up, expressive

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Identity payoff — 'feel like a person' is the emotional end-state, bigger than any biomarker

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I still have good days and bad days. Everyone does.
Sunny outdoor selfie, sunglasses, pine trees, drink in hand

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Anti-hype credibility — admitting bad days makes the claim survivable

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: But my bad days now are not even close to what my regular days were before. I'm not flat anymore.
Flashback: woman under a blanket rubbing her eyes

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Contrast anchor — one last look at 'before' so the after lands

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I'm not staring at my phone for an hour wondering where my motivation went.
Older woman frowning at her phone at the counter

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Negative-litany callback 1 — each 'I'm not...' un-does an Act 2 scene

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: I'm not watching my to-do list pile up while I do nothing about it. And I didn't have to give up a single pound to get there.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: Negative-litany callback 2 + the guarantee that matters: zero weight-loss sacrifice

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So if you're on GLP-1 and something feels off, it's not in your head. Very likely it's your receptors, and there is a fix that doesn't touch your weight loss.
Woman walking tall through a sunlit garden, flowers in hand

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: CTA by diagnosis — 'it's not in your head, it's your receptors' hands the viewer a reason AND an out. Ends on motion + light
NOTES

cards.title: STRUCTURE
cards.text: 4:18, single continuous VO, ~40 cutaways. Every claim gets its own demo visual within ~1s of being spoken. Talking head is connective tissue only; the b-roll carries the persuasion. Cut rhythm: ~3s in story sections, slower (5-8s) during the mechanism explanation.

cards.title: B-ROLL CASTING TRICK
cards.text: The cutaways deliberately use MANY different women, ages ~35-70, different homes and body types. No continuity with the narrator, and it doesn't matter at this cut speed. Effect: every woman watching finds herself in at least one clip. Steal this.

cards.title: COMPLIANCE — DO NOT COPY
cards.text: The journal screenshot (0:34), the 4-headline news collage (2:09), and both Reddit threads (3:05, 3:12) are fabricated mockups with fake outlets and fake engagement. That tactic is noted for understanding only. Our versions never invent studies, publications, or threads. Hard law.

cards.title: WHAT TO STEAL
cards.text: 1) 'Sadness has texture, I was flat' language. 2) Receptor-sensitivity mechanism that explains why-her-not-me without attacking the drug. 3) Not-5-pills consolidation angle. 4) The wanting-to-cook-dinner transformation beat (desire returns, appetite stays suppressed). 5) The 'I'm not...' negative litany that un-does each Act 2 scene in reverse.

cards.title: PRODUCT RESTRAINT
cards.text: Product named at 3:12 by a fake Reddit stranger, shown once as a single capsule at 3:46. Zero pack shots, zero price, zero offer. The entire ad sells the DIAGNOSIS; the landing page (survey.zafiraorganics.com/flatness) sells the product.
